newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom IPO at 175 francs safe bet.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom IPO at 175 francs safe bet.

text.p: The French state would make a safe bet in the partial privatisation of France Telecom SA if it sold stock at 175 francs ($30.06) per share in the Initial Public Offering (IPO), financial data showed on Tuesday.

Data in Reuters Securities 3000 showed that the price would allow the government to raise its intended 50 billion francs while at the same time allowing for a future rise of the share price to the pleasure of shareholders.
Priced at a relative low price/earnings multiple compared with other telecommunications groups, the government also has some leeway in case the world's stock markets fall.
On Monday, financial analysts said France Telecom SA was worth some 150 billion to 200 billion francs and added they expected an IPO price of 175 francs.
The Finance Ministry will announce on May 5 the price range in what could become the country's biggest market flotation ever. The final price will be set on the evening of May 26.
At an IPO price of 175 francs, and using ABN AMRO Hoare Govett's estimate of 1997 France Telecom results of 14 billion francs, the share would be priced at a 1997 price/earnings multiple of 12.5.
That is one of the lowest multiples in the telecommunications sector, according to Reuters Securities 3000.
The ratio for main telecommunications companies ranges from NTT's 63.87 to AT&T Corp's 9.15.
Stripping out NTT, the average for 14 listed telecommunications companies is 17.6.
The average P/E for French blue-chip companies in the CAC-40 index at April 14 closing prices was 23.21.
The recent volatility of the share markets, with Paris following Wall Street's gyrations, may cause some palpitations among the country's mandarins concerning the fate of France's biggest share sale.
But data show that overall share markets would have to fall by 30 percent to bring the average P/E to 12.3 and thus below France Telecom's IPO P/E.
France Telecom plans to pay out 45 percent of earnings in dividends. Using the 14 billion francs as a basis this would give 6.3 billion francs, or 6.3 francs per share for a yield of 3.6 percent.
The average dividend yield for 15 telecommunications companies is 3.18 percent. Excluding NTT it is 3.37 percent.
Analysts said that France Telecom's share could rise to 225 francs within a year, which would represent a 28.5 percent gain.

The Finance Ministry, which aims to raise between 30 billion and 50 billion from the sale of a minority stake in France Telecom, could at 175 francs per share raise 52.5 billion francs with a 30 percent stake.

France Telecom Chairman Michel Bon has said that the placement could involve a stake of between 30 and 40 percent of the company's capital. At 40 percent, the 175 franc price would yield France 70 billion francs.
